title: The partner slice of RWB-E1-032 and its target service frame are not stated in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 032 Automatic attach from the OCR intake v1.md (module P5 Document hub); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R4, R5.2 and R6; _work/msr/context/S9.md
section: Metadata Service and Service epic; Section 1 Story; Section 2 Business rationale
description: The legacy story is a P5 Document hub story and no source states that automatic attach has a partner half or that rwb-partner (S9) carries one. This run's split plan and the work package place a secondary slice in S9, so the story is written on the rwb-partner frame: schema rwb_partner, base /api/recovery/partner/v1, topic rwb.partner.events.v1, queue rwb-partner and package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner. Neither the slice boundary nor the frame is published.
evidence: Legacy story line 12 reads 'Module | P5 Document hub'; its section 4 flow is the JOB-12 matcher and its section 12 operations are the document-hub intake operations. Arch v5 slide 4 places S9 rwb-partner in the shared capabilities group for partner management only and no slide names an intake or attach operation on S9.
proposed: Confirm the secondary partner slice in the Change Register and publish the S9 frame for RWB-S9-E1032-APP in the Service Contract Catalog; until then the story stands on the Template R4 naming rules and cites this row.

title: The partner-origin channel of an intake item and its attach state are a boundary no source states
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (A2.5 Receive a partner result into the case; Screens); Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2 (T5.1, T5.3); legacy RWB-E1-032 section 2
section: Section 1 Story; Section 4 Flow; Section 5 Exception paths; Section 9 State transitions
description: No source says how a partner file reaches the OCR intake with its instruction and case, whether the partner service keeps a submission row, or how the attach outcome returns to the partner. This story fixes that boundary: a submission row in rwb_partner holding the firm, the instruction, the case hint, the type, the hash, the intake item ID and the state; one fact PartnerDocumentSubmitted; the attach event and the item read back. Every element is this story's design and none is a published value.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.5 covers a contact, promise or cash result on the case and names no document submission; TSD S9 T5.1 names INT-24 Partner portal for screens only and T5.3 names InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted; the legacy story section 2 names 'partner files' as one of three unnamed sources and carries no partner column.
proposed: Publish the partner file channel in the S9 contract baseline: the submission row, the PartnerDocumentSubmitted fact, the attach event consumed and the item read used to copy the match state.

title: Wave conflict: EP01 puts this story in wave 1 while rwb-partner is wave 4 in Arch v5
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.6; _work/msr/context/S9.md service row; split_plan.json RWB-S9-E1032-APP
description: R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave where it is earlier than the service wave, so the story stays in wave 1 with release 30 November 2026 (tentative) although Arch v5 puts rwb-partner in wave 4. One conflict row is raised for S9 and EP01.
evidence: Template R5.6 wave map: EP01 = 1; context pack S9 service row: Wave 4; work package slice: wave 1, release 30 November 2026.
proposed: Keep wave 1 and the unchanged tentative release as R5.6 requires; confirm at the wave 1 entry check that the S9 frame and its platform baseline are available to a wave 1 story.

title: The DP table names platform H rows that the plan's H list does not carry
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 and R5.7; split_plan.json RWB-S9-E1032-APP
section: Metadata Depends on (build); Section 13 Solution plan
description: DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 each add an H row on a platform contract (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON). The work package fixes H empty for this slice, so the story applies the patterns with those rows held as the wave-0 shared baseline and records them here rather than as H.
evidence: Template R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; work package story line H []; plan slice RWB-S9-E1032-APP H [].
proposed: Keep the H list as the work package fixes it and record the seven platform rows as the shared baseline of wave 0; revisit only if a platform contract is not published before the wave 1 entry check.

title: The two partner submission operations, the intake creation path and the PartnerDocumentSubmitted event are not published
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2 (Appendix T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 S9 rows; _work/msr/context/S9.md Events; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 12
description: No source names POST or GET /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents, the document-hub operation that creates an intake item for a partner file, the payload of rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1, or the 404 and 409 bodies. The story fixes these shapes as its design; they must be published by the S9 contract baseline and the P5 contract before Done.
evidence: TSD S9 T-A.1 lists six operations, none for documents; the S9 ownership rows list GET /partner/instructions, GET /partners, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, POST accept, invoices and results only; the context pack names EV-20 and EV-21 without event names; the legacy story section 12 publishes document-hub intake endpoints and no partner operation.
proposed: Publish the two operations, the intake creation and the PartnerDocumentSubmitted payload in RWB-S9-E1032-CON and the document-hub intake creation in the P5 contract, with the 404 and 409 bodies and the RFC 9457 problem shape.

title: The intake bound, the decision code and version, and the two lists in force are not named
source: legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 3 and 8; Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2 T3.2; FSD S9 A2.5
section: Section 3 Preconditions; Section 12.2; Section 13 Configuration and reference data; Section 14
description: The story reads an intake bound parameter, the decision code of the acceptance with the version in force, and LOV-DOC-TYPE with LOV-INSTR-STATUS. No source names the parameter row, the decision code, the version or LOV-DOC-TYPE, so the story uses the placeholder and invents no value.
evidence: The legacy section 3 names CASE_NO_PATTERN, ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD in document_hub_parameter, none of which is an intake bound; TSD T3.2 lists LOV-INSTR-STATUS, LOV-INSTRUCTION, LOV-PANEL and LOV-PARTNER-TYPE and no document type list; the legacy section 8 BR5 names principle 5 and R-UNI-39 without a decision code.
proposed: Publish the intake bound parameter row, the acceptance decision code with its version and LOV-DOC-TYPE in the S9 reference data set, and keep every value out of code.

title: No data model carries a partner-side submission row
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 11
description: partner_intake is created by this story with id, partner_id, instruction_id, case_id, document_type, file_sha256, intake_item_id, state, candidate_case_ids, received_at, the standard audit columns and version. No LDM or TSD entity holds it, so the column names and types are the story's design and no field ID is allocated.
evidence: TSD S9 T3.1 defines partner, partner_instruction and partner_user only (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016); the legacy section 11 writes document_intake fields DF-DOC-075, DF-DOC-076, DF-DOC-060 and DF-DOC-061, which belong to P5 and are not this service's.
proposed: Add partner_intake to the LDM and the physical schema rwb_partner with its field IDs before the wave 1 entry check; until then the story's migration is the only definition.

title: No source states how the legacy criteria split between the document-hub and partner slices
source: legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 7 and 16; split_plan.json RWB-E1-032 and RWB-S9-E1032-APP
section: Section 7 Acceptance criteria; Section 16 Test cases
description: All fifteen legacy criteria AC1 to AC15 and the seventeen legacy test cases describe the matcher, the store and the reviewer and stay word for word with RWB-P5-E1032-APP. This slice therefore owns no legacy criterion and writes seven new criteria with eight new test cases; the split is this run's ruling, recorded here, not a source statement.
evidence: Legacy section 7 AC1 to AC15 and section 16 TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-17; the plan slice row RWB-S9-E1032-APP carries acs [] while the RWB-P5-E1032-APP slice carries the legacy ids.
proposed: Record the primary/secondary AC split in the AC Glossary and the RTM so the fifteen legacy criteria are counted once, against RWB-P5-E1032-APP.

title: The partner portal screen that submits a file is not fixed
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 Screens table; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 15
description: FSD S9 lists PRT-01 Partner home, PRT-02 Instruction, PRT-03 Upload result and PRT-04 Invoice with First in E2, E4 and E6, and no source states which screen carries the document submission of an instruction. The story names the service answer only and leaves the screen number open.
evidence: FSD S9 Screens table rows PRT-01 to PRT-04; the legacy section 15 names SCR-31 Document review queue and SCR-30 Case documents only, both document-hub screens.
proposed: Fix the screen that carries the submission when PRT-02 Instruction is specified, and keep the service answer unchanged.
